question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I went to the lake and ______ some of its water in my metallic cup.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. drank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence has two verbs joined by the conjunction "and": "went" and the blank. By the rule of parallelism, both verbs must be in the same tense — "went" is simple past, so the blank needs the V2 (past) form. (समानान्तरता)

◦ The verb forms of "drink" are: drink (V1) – drank (V2) – drunk (V3).

◦ Correct: I went to the lake and drank some of its water in my metallic cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "drinking" is a present participle; it cannot stand alone as a finite verb without a helping verb (was/is drinking).

• Option 3 "drunk" is the past participle (V3) and needs "have/had" before it.

• Option 4 "drunken" is an adjective used only before a noun (a drunken brawl), never as a main verb.

NOTE

• Similar V1–V2–V3 sets often asked: sink–sank–sunk, ring–rang–rung, swim–swam–swum, begin–began–begun.

• Remember: "drunk" describes the state of intoxication (He is drunk); "drunken" is attributive (a drunken driver).

question: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Occurred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Occurred is the correctly spelt word. "Occur" ends in a stressed consonant–vowel–consonant, so the final r doubles before -ed/-ing: occur → occurred, occurring, occurrence. (घटित होना)

◦ Correct: The accident occurred late at night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is misspelt; the correct spelling is Indispensable (absolutely necessary).

• Option 2 is misspelt; the correct spelling is Liaison (a link/communication between groups).

• Option 3 is misspelt; the correct spelling is Privilege (a special right) — note there is no "d" and it ends in -lege.

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt SSC words: accommodation, embarrassment, maintenance, questionnaire, harassment, committee, conscience, definitely.

• Doubling rule also applies to: refer → referred, prefer → preferred, begin → beginning, permit → permitted.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Gut Feeling
option_1: To have a dispute with someone
option_2: A personal intuition you get, especially when feel something may not be right
option_3: Very excited and/or joyful, especially when in love
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A personal intuition you get, especially when feel something may not be right.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "gut feeling" means an instinctive feeling or intuition not based on reason or evidence — an inner hunch, especially a warning that something is wrong. (अंतर्ज्ञान / अंदरूनी अहसास)

◦ Correct: I had a gut feeling that the deal would fall through, and it did.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to have a dispute with someone" matches idioms like at loggerheads or cross swords, not "gut feeling".

• Option 3 "very excited and/or joyful, especially when in love" corresponds to on cloud nine or head over heels.

• Option 4 "doing things recklessly" corresponds to throwing caution to the wind.

NOTE

• Related "gut" idioms: gut reaction (immediate instinctive response), hate someone's guts (dislike intensely), spill one's guts (confess everything), bust a gut (work extremely hard).

question:
Identify the segment that contains grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

George handing the / hairpin to Ron, a moment later.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. George handing the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence has no finite verb. "Handing" is a present participle (V1+ing) and cannot work as the main verb of a sentence on its own. (मुख्य क्रिया का अभाव)

◦ Since the time reference is past ("a moment later"), the past-tense finite verb handed is required.

◦ Correct: George handed the hairpin to Ron, a moment later.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "hairpin to Ron," is correct — "hand something to someone" is the standard pattern.

• Option 3 "a moment later." is a correct adverbial phrase of time.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the sentence is a fragment without part 1 being corrected.

NOTE

• A clause needs a finite verb; -ing forms need an auxiliary (is/was/has been) to become finite: "George was handing…".

• Common SSC trap: replacing a finite verb with a participle, e.g. "He going to school daily" (✗) → "He goes to school daily" (✓).

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: He supposed he shuld be thankful.
option_2: He supposed he should be thankful.
option_3: He supposed he should be thankfull.
option_4: He suposed he should be thankful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He supposed he should be thankful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 2 spells all three key words correctly — supposed, should and thankful. (आभारी)

◦ The suffix -ful (meaning 'full of') always has a single l: thank + ful = thankful.

◦ Correct: He supposed he should be thankful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "should" as shuld (the 'o' is dropped).

• Option 3 misspells "thankful" as thankfull (double l is wrong).

• Option 4 misspells "supposed" as suposed (the 'p' must be doubled).

NOTE

• Adjective suffix -ful takes one l: beautiful, careful, useful, successful, grateful. But the adverb takes -fully: carefully, beautifully.

• Words with doubled letters often tested: success, occasion, possess, embarrass, accommodate.

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

Our financial situation had become (precarious).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Stable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Precarious means unstable, insecure, uncertain, likely to collapse or fail. (अनिश्चित / जोखिम भरा)

◦ Its exact opposite is Stable, meaning firm, secure and not likely to change or fail. (स्थिर)

◦ Correct: Our financial situation had become precarious, but after the new contract it turned stable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Insecure" (not safe/confident) is a synonym of precarious, not an antonym.

• Option 3 "Delicate" (fragile, easily damaged) is also close in sense to precarious.

• Option 4 "Noisy" (full of noise) is unrelated to the idea of stability.

NOTE

• Synonyms of precarious: risky, perilous, shaky, hazardous, uncertain, dicey.

• Antonyms of precarious: stable, secure, safe, certain, steady, firm.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

The medieval forerunner of chemistry
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Alchemy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alchemy is the medieval forerunner (early form) of chemistry, chiefly concerned with turning base metals into gold and finding the elixir of life. (कीमियागरी / रसायन विद्या)

◦ A person who practised it was called an alchemist.

◦ Correct: Alchemy was the medieval forerunner of chemistry.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Anthropologist — one who studies human societies, cultures and their development.

• Option 2 Curator — the keeper or in-charge of a museum or art gallery.

• Option 4 Anchor — a heavy device that holds a ship in place; also a person who presents a TV programme.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Astrology — the forerunner of astronomy; Numismatics — study of coins; Philately — stamp collecting; Archivist — keeper of records.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I'm recovering from the flu, and I still is feeling weak.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. feel weak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the underlined clause is "I", which never takes "is". By subject–verb agreement, "I" takes the base verb feel. (कर्ता-क्रिया सामंजस्य)

◦ "Feel" here is a linking verb, so it must be followed by the adjective "weak", not an adverb or a past participle.

◦ Correct: I'm recovering from the flu, and I still feel weak.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "I … is feeling" is clearly ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "feels weakened" wrongly uses the third-person singular "feels" with "I".

• Option 3 "felt weakest" shifts to past tense and uses a superlative without any comparison group, clashing with the present-tense "I'm recovering".

NOTE

• Linking verbs (feel, look, seem, taste, smell, sound, appear) are followed by adjectives: "It tastes sweet" (✓), not "sweetly".

• "I" takes am/was/have/do; it never takes is/has/does.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Subtle
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Exquisite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Subtle means delicate, fine, refined or so precise as to be hard to notice. (सूक्ष्म / बारीक)

◦ Exquisite means extremely beautiful, delicate and finely made — the closest match among the given options. (अति सुंदर / उत्कृष्ट)

◦ Correct: The painting showed a subtle/exquisite blending of colours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Corrupt — dishonest, morally depraved; unrelated to fineness.

• Option 2 Homely — plain or ordinary (in American usage, unattractive); the opposite of refined.

• Option 4 Wrong — incorrect or unjust; no connection with delicacy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of subtle: delicate, nuanced, understated, faint, refined, elusive.

• Antonyms of subtle: obvious, blatant, crude, glaring, coarse.

• Note the silent b in "subtle" (pronounced /ˈsʌt(ə)l/), like in doubt, debt, comb.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The cat sits in the window and staring at the squirrel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. stares at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two verbs joined by "and" must be parallel in form and tense. The first verb is "sits" (simple present, third person singular), so the second must also be "stares". (समानान्तरता)

◦ The correct preposition after "stare" when looking fixedly at something is at: *stare at*.

◦ Correct: The cat sits in the window and stares at the squirrel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "sits … and staring" breaks parallelism.

• Option 3 "stare on" uses the wrong preposition and the wrong verb form for the singular subject "the cat".

• Option 4 "stared at" is past tense and does not match the present-tense "sits".

NOTE

• Fixed prepositions with verbs of looking: stare at, glance at, gaze at, peep into, look into (investigate), look after (take care of).

• Parallelism rule: "She likes swimming and cycling" (✓), not "swimming and to cycle".

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A long wandering or voyage usually marked by many changes of fortune
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Odyssey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An odyssey is a long, eventful journey or wandering full of changes of fortune and adventure. (लंबी साहसिक यात्रा)

◦ The word comes from Homer's Greek epic *The Odyssey*, describing Odysseus's ten-year voyage home from Troy.

◦ Correct: His ten-year search for his family was a true odyssey.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Ode — a lyric poem written in praise of a person, thing or event.

• Option 3 Pilgrimage — a journey made to a sacred or holy place for religious reasons.

• Option 4 Trip — an ordinary short journey; it lacks the sense of long wandering and changing fortunes.

NOTE

• Journey-related one-word substitutions: Voyage — journey by sea; Itinerary — plan/record of a journey; Expedition — organised journey with a purpose; Sojourn — a temporary stay.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Fear evolved over millions of years to protect us from ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. danger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence talks about the evolutionary purpose of fear. Fear is a survival instinct that warns living beings of threats, so it protects us from danger. (खतरा)

◦ The collocation "protect somebody from danger" is the standard and logical pairing.

◦ Correct: Fear evolved over millions of years to protect us from danger.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "birth" is illogical — fear does not protect anyone from being born.

• Option 3 "confidence" is a positive quality; one does not need protection from it.

• Option 4 "courage" is also positive and is in fact the opposite pole of fear, so it cannot be what fear protects us from.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with protect: protect from/against harm, danger, infection, attack.

• Related vocabulary: peril (serious danger), hazard (a risk), jeopardy (danger of loss or harm), menace (a threat).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The plan began to ______ once we all met to discuss it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. jell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb jell means to take definite shape, to come together successfully — exactly what a plan does when people discuss it. (आकार लेना / मूर्त रूप लेना)

◦ It is used both literally (a liquid setting into jelly) and figuratively (ideas, plans or teams coming together).

◦ Correct: The plan began to jell once we all met to discuss it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "jail" means to imprison someone — a plan cannot be jailed.

• Option 2 "gel" as a noun is a thick semi-solid substance (hair gel); the official key here treats jell as the verb form required.

• Option 4 "gale" is a noun meaning a very strong wind; it is not a verb.

NOTE

• "Jell" is chiefly American; British English also allows gel as the verb, but SSC keys follow the spelling jell for 'take shape'.

• Similar figurative verbs: crystallise (become clear/definite), shape up, fall into place.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Calm
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Frenzy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Calm means peaceful, quiet and free from agitation or excitement. (शांत)

◦ Frenzy means a state of wild, uncontrolled excitement or agitation, which is the exact opposite of calm. (उन्माद / उत्तेजना)

◦ Correct: The crowd went from calm to a frenzy the moment the star appeared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Harmonious" means peaceful and free from conflict — close in sense to calm, not opposite.

• Option 3 "Placid" means not easily upset or excited — a direct synonym of calm.

• Option 4 "Low-key" means restrained and not showy — again similar to calm, not its antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of calm: serene, tranquil, composed, placid, unruffled, sedate.

• Antonyms of calm: frenzy, agitation, turmoil, tumult, uproar, stormy, frantic.

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

Although Shagun was competently doing the project on her own, Pranav couldn't stop himself from (giving her unnecessary advice).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. being a backseat driver.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A backseat driver is a person who gives unwanted advice or instructions about something he/she is not responsible for. (बिन मांगी सलाह देने वाला)

◦ The context — Shagun was managing well but Pranav kept advising her — matches this idiom precisely.

◦ Correct: Although Shagun was competently doing the project on her own, Pranav couldn't stop himself from being a backseat driver.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 devil's advocate — one who argues the opposite view merely for the sake of debate.

• Option 3 a bitter pill to swallow — an unpleasant fact or situation that must be accepted.

• Option 4 cut the mustard — to reach the required standard or perform satisfactorily.

NOTE

• Related idioms: breathe down someone's neck (watch too closely), poke one's nose into (interfere), call the shots (be in charge).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(The transit of the Planet of Love happen in pairs), eight years apart every century.
option_1: The transits of the Planet of Love happen in pairs
option_3: The transits of the Planet of Love happens at pairs
option_4: The transit of Planet of Love happen in pairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The transits of the Planet of Love happen in pairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "in pairs" and "eight years apart" shows that more than one transit is being described, so the subject must be plural — transits. (पारगमन)

◦ A plural subject takes the plural verb happen (no -s), and the correct idiom is happen in pairs, not 'at pairs'.

◦ Correct: The transits of the Planet of Love happen in pairs, eight years apart every century.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the singular "transit" clashes with the plural verb "happen" and with "in pairs".

• Option 3 wrongly pairs the plural subject "transits" with the singular verb "happens" and uses the wrong preposition "at pairs".

• Option 4 keeps the singular "transit" with the plural verb "happen" and also drops the required article "the" before "Planet of Love".

NOTE

• Rule: plural subject + plural verb (V1); singular subject + singular verb (V1+s/es).

• The definite article the is used before unique/named objects: the Sun, the Earth, the Planet of Love (Venus).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I am not going to help you of this science project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. help you of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb help takes the preposition with when referring to the task in which assistance is given: *help someone with something*. The preposition "of" is wrong here. (सहायता करना)

◦ "Help" can also be followed by in + V-ing (help him in completing the work) or by a bare/to-infinitive (help him finish).

◦ Correct: I am not going to help you with this science project.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "I am not going to" is correct — 'be going to' is a standard structure for near-future intention.

• Option 3 "this science project." is a correct noun phrase with the demonstrative "this".

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the preposition in part 1 is clearly incorrect.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositions: help with, assist in/with, deal with, cope with, provide with, supply with.

• Note the difference: deprive of, accuse of, suspect of — these take "of", but "help" does not.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Consensus
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Agreement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Consensus means a general or collective agreement reached by a group. (सर्वसम्मति)

◦ Hence Agreement — the state of concurring in opinion — is its exact synonym.

◦ Correct: After hours of debate, the committee finally reached a consensus (an agreement).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Census — the official counting of a country's population (a confusable near-homophone of consensus).

• Option 2 Censure — strong disapproval or formal criticism.

• Option 3 Puck — a hard rubber disc used in ice hockey; also a mischievous sprite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of consensus: unanimity, accord, concurrence, harmony, common consent.

• Antonyms: disagreement, dissent, discord, contention.

• Distinguish: censure (criticise) vs censor (ban/cut objectionable content) vs census (population count).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

I watched him with the excitement of ______ him to do anything at any time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. expecting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Expect means to anticipate or think that something will happen. "The excitement of expecting him to do anything at any time" conveys eager anticipation, which fits the word "excitement". (अपेक्षा करना / प्रत्याशा)

◦ "Expect" takes the pattern expect + object + to-infinitive: *expect him to do*. Also, the preposition "of" must be followed by a gerund (V1+ing).

◦ Correct: I watched him with the excitement of expecting him to do anything at any time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lacking" means being without something; "lacking him to do" is not a valid structure.

• Option 2 "excepting" means excluding/leaving out and does not fit the sense of excitement.

• Option 4 "accepting" means agreeing to receive; it would not create excitement about unpredictable action.

NOTE

• Confusables: except (exclude) vs accept (receive/agree) vs expect (anticipate).

• Preposition + gerund rule: "the idea of going", "fond of singing", "insist on paying".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Humans have rapidly changing the balance of gases in the atmosphere.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. changing the balance of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The auxiliary "have" must be followed by the past participle (V3) to form the present perfect tense. Therefore "changing" must become changed. (पूर्ण वर्तमान काल)

◦ Structure: Subject + have/has + V3 → Humans have changed…

◦ Correct: Humans have rapidly changed the balance of gases in the atmosphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Humans have rapidly" is correct — the plural subject "Humans" rightly takes "have", and the adverb "rapidly" is correctly placed after the auxiliary.

• Option 3 "gases in the atmosphere." is correct — "gases" is the proper plural of "gas" and "the atmosphere" takes the definite article.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because part 2 breaks the have + V3 rule.

NOTE

• If a continuous sense were intended, the form would be "have been changing" (present perfect continuous).

• Quick check: have/has/had + V3; is/am/are/was/were + V1+ing.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I was surprised— (1) ______ at the news that my father spared me any thought, and second at my brother's compliment, (2) ______ it was backhanded. Dhri (3) ______ commented on my looks; nor did he encourage me to comment on his. Such useless (4) ______, he believed, made people vain. Was this another (5) ______ of change?

SubQuestion No : 21

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. first.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence lists two causes of surprise and the second one is explicitly introduced by "and second at my brother's compliment". The correlative pair required is first … second. (सर्वप्रथम … दूसरे)

◦ Enumerating adverbs must match in form: first/second, firstly/secondly.

◦ Correct: I was surprised— first at the news that my father spared me any thought, and second at my brother's compliment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "earlier" indicates a comparison of time, not an item in a list.

• Option 3 "in the beginning" refers to the start of a period or story, and does not pair with "second".

• Option 4 "second" would repeat the ordinal already used later in the sentence, making the list illogical.

NOTE

• Common enumerating sets: first … second … third … finally; firstly … secondly … lastly.

• Keep parallel form throughout a list — do not mix "first" with "secondly".

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I was surprised— (1) ______ at the news that my father spared me any thought, and second at my brother's compliment, (2) ______ it was backhanded. Dhri (3) ______ commented on my looks; nor did he encourage me to comment on his. Such useless (4) ______, he believed, made people vain. Was this another (5) ______ of change?

SubQuestion No : 22

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. though.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There is a contrast between being pleased by a compliment and the compliment being backhanded (an insult disguised as praise). A contrast needs the conjunction though (= although / even if). (यद्यपि)

◦ Correct: … and second at my brother's compliment, though it was backhanded.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "afterwards" is an adverb of time and shows sequence, not contrast.

• Option 2 "all" is a determiner/quantifier and cannot join two clauses.

• Option 3 "through" is a preposition meaning 'from one side to the other'; it is a common spelling confusion with "though" but cannot introduce a clause.

NOTE

• Contrast connectors: though, although, even though, whereas, while, yet, however, nevertheless.

• Distinguish the look-alikes: though (although), through (across), thorough (complete), thought (past of think), tough (hard).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I was surprised— (1) ______ at the news that my father spared me any thought, and second at my brother's compliment, (2) ______ it was backhanded. Dhri (3) ______ commented on my looks; nor did he encourage me to comment on his. Such useless (4) ______, he believed, made people vain. Was this another (5) ______ of change?

SubQuestion No : 23

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. never.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The second half of the sentence, "nor did he encourage me to comment on his", carries a negative idea. The correlative neither/never … nor requires a negative in the first clause, so never is needed. (कभी नहीं)

◦ Correct: Dhri never commented on my looks; nor did he encourage me to comment on his.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "always" is positive and would contradict the following "nor" clause.

• Option 3 "forever" means for all time; it is also positive and does not collocate with "nor".

• Option 4 "ever" is used mainly in questions, negatives and conditionals ("Have you ever…?"); alone in an affirmative statement it is ungrammatical here.

NOTE

• After "nor", the clause takes inversion: nor did he encourage, nor was she willing.

• Negative correlatives: neither … nor, not only … but also, hardly … when, no sooner … than.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I was surprised— (1) ______ at the news that my father spared me any thought, and second at my brother's compliment, (2) ______ it was backhanded. Dhri (3) ______ commented on my looks; nor did he encourage me to comment on his. Such useless (4) ______, he believed, made people vain. Was this another (5) ______ of change?

SubQuestion No : 24

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. talk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank refers back to the commenting on one another's looks described in the previous sentence. Such conversation is best summed up as "such useless talk". (बेकार की बातचीत)

◦ "Talk" is an uncountable noun here, so it correctly follows the determiner "such useless" without an article.

◦ Correct: Such useless talk, he believed, made people vain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ode" is a poem of praise — a specific literary form, not everyday conversation.

• Option 2 "disclosure" means revealing secret information; nothing secret was revealed.

• Option 3 "babble" means meaningless chatter; it is close in tone but does not fit the deliberate compliments described, and "useless babble" would be redundant.

NOTE

• Words for speech: chatter (idle talk), banter (playful teasing), discourse (formal discussion), prattle (childish talk), rhetoric (persuasive speech).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I was surprised— (1) ______ at the news that my father spared me any thought, and second at my brother's compliment, (2) ______ it was backhanded. Dhri (3) ______ commented on my looks; nor did he encourage me to comment on his. Such useless (4) ______, he believed, made people vain. Was this another (5) ______ of change?

SubQuestion No : 25

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. sign.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A sign means an indication or evidence that something is happening. The narrator wonders whether her brother's unusual compliment was one more indication of change. (संकेत / लक्षण)

◦ The collocation "a sign of" is standard: a sign of change, a sign of trouble, a sign of hope.

◦ Correct: Was this another sign of change?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "signature" is a person's name written by himself/herself — it does not indicate change.

• Option 3 "light" does not collocate with "of change" in this sense; "in the light of" is a different idiom.

• Option 4 "symbolic" is an adjective, but the structure "another ______ of" needs a noun.

NOTE

• Similar nouns of indication: hint, indication, token, symptom, omen, portent.

• Useful phrases: a sign of the times, show signs of, no sign of.

question: Which among the following is a traditional Hindu festival centered on the Goddess Mahakali from Telangana, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bonalu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bonalu is a traditional Hindu folk festival of Telangana dedicated to the Goddess Mahakali. (बोनालु — तेलंगाना का लोक पर्व)

• The word *Bonam* means bhojanam (meal) — women carry cooked rice with milk and jaggery in decorated earthen pots on their heads as an offering to the Mother Goddess.

• It is celebrated in the month of Ashada (July–August), most famously at the Sri Jagadambika temple in Golconda Fort, Ujjaini Mahankali temple in Secunderabad and the Balkampet Yellamma temple, Hyderabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dehing Patkai — a festival (and also a rainforest/national park) of Assam, held in the Dehing Patkai region of Upper Assam.

• Ugadi — the New Year festival of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, marking the beginning of the Chaitra month; the special dish is *Ugadi Pachadi*.

• Lohri — a harvest/bonfire festival of Punjab celebrated on 13 January, marking the end of winter and the harvesting of the rabi crop.

NOTE

• Other Telangana festivals: Bathukamma (floral festival of Goddess Gauri, a State festival), Sammakka Saralamma Jatara (Medaram, Asia's largest tribal fair).

• Quick match: Bihu — Assam; Onam — Kerala; Pongal — Tamil Nadu; Hornbill — Nagaland; Wangala — Meghalaya.

question: Kumari Kamala was awarded with Padma Bhushan in 1970. She was recognized for which classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kumari Kamala (Kamala Lakshman, popularly "Baby Kamala") was a celebrated exponent of Bharatanatyam and was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 1970. (भरतनाट्यम)

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, rooted in the *Natya Shastra* of Bharata Muni and in the temple *Devadasi* tradition; it is often called the "fire dance".

• Its repertoire follows the *Margam* order — Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mohiniyattam — classical dance of Kerala, the "dance of the enchantress"; exponents: Sunanda Nair, Kalamandalam Kshemavathy, Bharati Shivaji.

• Manipuri — classical dance of Manipur, based on Ras Leela of Radha–Krishna; exponents: the Jhaveri Sisters, Guru Bipin Singh.

• Kathak — classical dance of Uttar Pradesh; exponents: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj.

NOTE

• Eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Famous Bharatanatyam dancers: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Mallika Sarabhai.

question: The sepoys of Meerut arrived at the Gates of Red Fort to meet the Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11 May, 1857.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Revolt of 1857 broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857; the mutinous sepoys marched through the night and reached the gates of the Red Fort, Delhi on 11 May 1857 to meet Bahadur Shah II (Zafar). (1857 का विद्रोह)

• The sepoys proclaimed the aged Bahadur Shah Zafar the Shahenshah-e-Hindustan, giving the revolt a symbolic national leadership.

• The immediate cause was the greased cartridge of the new Enfield rifle; Mangal Pandey of the 34th Native Infantry had already revolted at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was hanged on 8 April 1857.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• After the revolt was crushed, Bahadur Shah Zafar was tried and deported to Rangoon (Burma), where he died in 1862 — ending the Mughal dynasty.

• Delhi was recaptured by the British in September 1857; General John Nicholson was killed in the assault.

• The revolt led to the Government of India Act, 1858, transferring power from the East India Company to the British Crown.

NOTE

• Centres and leaders of 1857: Delhi — Bahadur Shah II / General Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb / Tantia Tope; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah.

• V.D. Savarkar called it the "First War of Indian Independence".

question: Which of the following countries is a part of 'I2U2' Summit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India, Israel, UAE and US.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• I2U2 stands for India, Israel, UAE and the United States — the two "I"s and the two "U"s. (आई2यू2 समूह)

• The grouping was formed in October 2021 as the "International Forum for Economic Cooperation"; the first virtual Leaders' Summit was held on 14 July 2022.

• Its focus areas are water, energy, transportation, space, health and food security; a flagship project is an integrated food park in Gujarat and a hybrid renewable energy project in Gujarat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• I2U2 is popularly called the "West Asian Quad" or "Middle-East Quad".

• The original Quad (QSD) consists of India, USA, Japan and Australia — an Indo-Pacific grouping.

• India–UAE signed the CEPA (Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement) in February 2022, which came into force on 1 May 2022.

NOTE

• Other groupings: BRICS — Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa; SCO — headquartered at Beijing; IBSA — India, Brazil, South Africa; BIMSTEC — headquartered at Dhaka.

• The Abraham Accords (2020) normalising Israel–UAE ties paved the way for the I2U2 grouping.

question: Vidushi Sharan Rani is famous for playing which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vidushi Sharan Rani Backliwal (1929–2008) was the first woman sarod player of India and was known as the "Sarod Rani". (सरोद)

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (1968) and the Padma Bhushan (1986), and donated her rare collection of instruments to the National Museum, Delhi (Sharan Rani Backliwal Gallery of Musical Instruments).

• The sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument of Hindustani classical music with a metal fingerboard and a skin-covered resonator.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Flute (Bansuri) — Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh, Rakesh Chaurasia.

• Sitar — Pt. Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Anoushka Shankar, Nikhil Banerjee.

• Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pt. Kishan Maharaj, Pt. Samta Prasad.

NOTE

• Other famous sarod players: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan, Buddhadev Das Gupta, Amaan and Ayaan Ali Bangash.

• Instrument–artist one-liners: Shehnai — Ustad Bismillah Khan; Santoor — Pt. Shivkumar Sharma; Sarangi — Pt. Ram Narayan; Violin — Dr. L. Subramaniam; Veena — S. Balachander, Chitti Babu; Mridangam — Palghat Mani Iyer.

question: Which among the following is the coldest planet in the solar system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uranus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uranus records the lowest temperature ever measured in the solar system's planets — about –224 °C (49 K) in its upper atmosphere, which is why it is called the coldest planet. (यूरेनस — सबसे ठंडा ग्रह)

• Unlike the other planets, Uranus radiates almost no internal heat; it is tilted at nearly 98° and therefore appears to "roll" on its side while orbiting the Sun.

• It is the seventh planet from the Sun, discovered by Sir William Herschel in 1781 — the first planet discovered with a telescope; it is an ice giant with a bluish-green colour due to methane.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Neptune — the farthest planet from the Sun and the windiest; its *average* temperature is marginally lower than that of Uranus, but its recorded minimum is higher.

• Saturn — the least dense planet (would float on water), famous for its bright ring system; largest moon Titan.

• Mars — the Red Planet, due to iron oxide; has the largest volcano Olympus Mons and moons Phobos and Deimos.

NOTE

• Superlatives: Hottest planet — Venus; largest — Jupiter; smallest — Mercury; fastest revolution — Mercury; densest — Earth; nearest to the Sun — Mercury.

• Venus and Uranus rotate from east to west (retrograde rotation).

• Some sources treat Neptune as the coldest on the basis of *mean* temperature; SSC's official key here marks Uranus, which is standard on the basis of the lowest recorded temperature.

question: The settlements in which large number of houses are built very close to each other are ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Compact settlements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a compact (nucleated / clustered) settlement, a large number of houses are built very close to each other, usually around a central point such as a temple, pond, well or crossroads. (सघन/गुच्छित बस्ती)

• Such settlements develop on fertile plains with adequate water supply — for example the Ganga plains, and are common where land is intensively cultivated.

• Settlements are broadly classified into rural and urban, and by pattern into compact and dispersed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dispersed (scattered) settlements — houses are spaced far apart, often separated by fields; typical of hills, forests, deserts and plateaus with rugged terrain.

• Linear settlements — houses are arranged in a line along a road, railway line, river bank or canal.

• Star settlements — develop where several roads converge, with houses spread out along the radiating roads.

NOTE

• Other settlement patterns: rectangular (in plains with a grid of roads), circular/semi-circular (around lakes or ponds), triangular (at the confluence of two rivers), T-shaped and Y-shaped (at road junctions).

• Temporary settlements — occupied for a short time, e.g. by nomads, shifting cultivators, lumberjacks; permanent settlements — inhabited round the year.

question: Which of the following Indian Players has scored maximum runs in Cricket World Cup 1983?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kapil Dev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kapil Dev was India's highest run-scorer in the 1983 Cricket World Cup with 303 runs, and he also led India to its first World Cup title. (कपिल देव)

• His unbeaten 175* off 138 balls against Zimbabwe at Tunbridge Wells (India were 17/5) is one of the most famous innings in World Cup history.

• India beat the West Indies by 43 runs in the final at Lord's on 25 June 1983; Mohinder Amarnath was the Man of the Match in both the semi-final and the final.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• K. Srikkanth — top-scored with 38 runs in the 1983 final; later captained India and chaired the national selection committee.

• Sunil Gavaskar — first batsman to score 10,000 Test runs and 34 Test centuries; he had a modest 1983 World Cup.

• Sandeep Patil — scored a fine 51* in the semi-final against England; later coached India and headed the selection panel.

NOTE

• Kapil Dev was the first player to take 400 Test wickets and was named Wisden Indian Cricketer of the Century (2002).

• India's World Cup wins: 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (MS Dhoni); T20 World Cup 2007 (MS Dhoni).

• The 1983 World Cup was hosted by England; it was the third edition and the last played with 60-over matches.

question: Which among the following is not an alkali metals and does not belong to the Group 1 of Periodic Table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Calcium (Ca, atomic number 20) is an alkaline earth metal belonging to Group 2, not Group 1; hence it is not an alkali metal. (क्षारीय मृदा धातु)

• Group 1 (alkali metals) consists of Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs and Fr; they have one electron in the outermost shell, are highly reactive, soft, and form strongly basic hydroxides.

• Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) consists of Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba and Ra, each with two valence electrons.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lithium (Li) — the lightest metal and the lightest solid element; widely used in Li-ion batteries.

• Sodium (Na) — kept immersed in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with air and water; common salt is NaCl.

• Potassium (K) — essential for nerve and muscle function; potassium reacts with water more violently than sodium.

NOTE

• Hydrogen is placed in Group 1 but is a non-metal, not an alkali metal.

• Reactivity of alkali metals increases down the group (Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs); Francium is radioactive.

• Calcium compounds: quicklime CaO, slaked lime Ca(OH)₂, limestone/marble CaCO₃, gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O, Plaster of Paris CaSO₄·½H₂O.

question: Who among the following is the first Indian to win the under 10 World Chess Championship in Menorca, Spain in the year 1996?
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} @font-face { font-family: 'Harikris'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARIKRIS.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>P Harikrishna
solution_text:
The correct answer is P Harikrishna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pentala Harikrishna became the first Indian to win the World Under-10 Chess Championship, held at Menorca, Spain in 1996. (पेंटाला हरिकृष्णा)

• He became India's youngest Grandmaster in 2001 (a record later broken), and won the World Junior Chess Championship in 2004.

• He hails from Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, and was awarded the Arjuna Award in 2005.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Koneru Humpy — from Andhra Pradesh; at 15 she became the then youngest woman ever to become a Grandmaster (2002); won the Women's World Rapid Championship in 2019 and 2024; Padma Shri and Arjuna Award recipient.

• Viswanathan Anand — India's first Grandmaster (1988), five-time World Chess Champion (2000, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2012), first recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (1991-92) and a Padma Vibhushan awardee.

• Vidit Santosh Gujrathi — Grandmaster from Nashik, Maharashtra; led the Indian team at the Chess Olympiad and won the FIDE Candidates-qualifying Grand Swiss 2023.

NOTE

• R. Praggnanandhaa, D. Gukesh, Arjun Erigaisi and Nihal Sarin are among India's leading young Grandmasters; D. Gukesh became World Chess Champion in 2024.

• Chess is believed to have originated in India as Chaturanga; FIDE (World Chess Federation) was founded in 1924 at Paris.

question: Which of the following has founded the city of Jaipur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sawai Jai Singh II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The city of Jaipur was founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber, who shifted his capital from Amber to Jaipur. (जयपुर की स्थापना)

• It was planned by the Bengali architect Vidyadhar Bhattacharya on the principles of the Shilpa Shastra/Vastu, making it India's first properly planned city; it is called the Pink City (painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales).

• Jaipur was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sawai Jai Singh II also built the five Jantar Mantar observatories at Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi; the Jaipur Jantar Mantar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2010).

• Prithviraj Chauhan — Chahamana ruler of Ajmer and Delhi who defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191) but was defeated in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).

• Raja Bharmal of Amber was the first Rajput ruler to form a matrimonial alliance with Akbar (1562); Raja Man Singh was Akbar's trusted general who led the Mughal army at the Battle of Haldighati (1576).

NOTE

• Jaipur landmarks: Hawa Mahal (built by Sawai Pratap Singh, 1799), City Palace, Amber Fort, Jaigarh and Nahargarh Forts, Albert Hall Museum.

• Rajasthan nicknames: Jaipur — Pink City; Jodhpur — Blue City; Udaipur — City of Lakes; Jaisalmer — Golden City.

question: In which of the following articles, "Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion" is mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 25.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 25 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality and health. (धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार)

• It falls under the Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28), which is part of the Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution.

• Explanation I of Article 25 states that wearing and carrying of kirpans shall be deemed to be included in the profession of the Sikh religion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 26 — freedom to manage religious affairs: every religious denomination may establish and maintain institutions, own property and administer it.

• Article 27 — freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion.

• Article 28 — freedom from attending religious instruction in educational institutions wholly maintained out of State funds.

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

• The word "secular" was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

• The Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment, 1978, and is now a legal right under Article 300A.

question: Which of the following is 'NOT' a feature of organic farming?
option_2: Minimal or no use of chemicals
solution_text:
The correct answer is No use of mixed cropping.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Organic farming actually encourages mixed cropping, inter-cropping and crop rotation to maintain soil fertility and control pests naturally — so "no use of mixed cropping" is not a feature of organic farming. (जैविक खेती)

• Organic farming is a system that avoids or largely excludes synthetic fertilisers, pesticides, growth regulators and feed additives, relying instead on organic inputs.

• It uses farmyard manure, compost, vermicompost, green manure, biofertilizers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, Blue-Green Algae, Mycorrhiza) and biopesticides (neem, Bacillus thuringiensis).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Minimal or no use of chemicals — the defining feature of organic farming; it keeps produce residue-free and prevents soil and water pollution.

• Use of recycled farm wastes — crop residues, cattle dung and other farm wastes are converted into compost, so nothing is wasted and the nutrient cycle is closed.

• Use of biofertilizers — living micro-organisms that fix atmospheric nitrogen or solubilise phosphorus, enriching the soil naturally.

NOTE

• Sikkim became India's first fully organic State (declared in 2016) and won the FAO's Future Policy Gold Award in 2018.

• Government schemes: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY, 2015), Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER), and the certification marks NPOP and Jaivik Bharat / India Organic.

question: The emblem of the Chera Dynasty that controlled the central and northern parts of Kerala and the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu was ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bow and arrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The emblem of the Chera dynasty was the bow and arrow; the Cheras ruled the central and northern parts of present-day Kerala and the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu. (चेर वंश का प्रतीक — धनुष-बाण)

• Their capital was Vanji (Karur/Kodungallur) and their chief ports were Muziris (Muchiri) and Tondi, famous for the Roman spice trade.

• The greatest Chera ruler was Senguttuvan (the Red Chera), who established the Pattini cult (worship of Kannagi); Ilango Adigal, the author of *Silappadikaram*, is associated with the Cheras.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chola emblem — the tiger; capital Uraiyur/Thanjavur/Gangaikonda Cholapuram; famous rulers Karikala, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I.

• Pandya emblem — the fish (twin carp); capital Madurai, port Korkai; famous for pearls and the Sangam assemblies.

• Pallava emblem — the bull; capital Kanchipuram; Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I were noted rulers.

NOTE

• The three crowned kings of the Tamil country (*Muvendar*) — Chera, Chola and Pandya — are mentioned in Ashoka's inscriptions.

• Sangam literature: *Tolkappiyam* (grammar), *Silappadikaram* (Ilango Adigal), *Manimekalai* (Sattanar), *Tirukkural* (Thiruvalluvar).

question: Banks are required to keep some reserves in liquid form with themselves. This is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Statutory liquidity ratio.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is the minimum percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that it must maintain with itself in the form of liquid assets — cash, gold, and approved government securities. (सांविधिक तरलता अनुपात)

• SLR is prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; it ensures bank solvency and also channels funds into government securities.

• In contrast, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the share of NDTL that banks must keep as cash with the RBI, and it earns no interest.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Open Market Operations (OMO) — the RBI's buying and selling of government securities in the open market to inject or absorb liquidity; it is a *quantitative* instrument of monetary policy.

• Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) — a window through which banks borrow overnight from the RBI against their SLR securities at a rate above the repo rate. ("Marginal stability scheme" is not a real term.)

• "Legal deposit ratio" is not an RBI instrument; the correct terms are CRR and SLR.

NOTE

• Quantitative tools of monetary policy: Bank Rate, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR, OMO, MSF, LAF.

• Repo rate — rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks; Reverse repo — rate at which the RBI borrows from banks.

• The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has 6 members (3 RBI + 3 government nominees) and is headed by the RBI Governor; inflation target: 4% (+/– 2%).

question: Sodium Hydroxide is the chemical name of which of the following common substances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Caustic Soda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is commonly known as caustic soda or lye; it is a strong alkali that is highly corrosive and deliquescent. (कास्टिक सोडा)

• It is manufactured by the chlor-alkali process — the electrolysis of brine (aqueous NaCl), which also yields chlorine at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.

• Uses: manufacture of soap and detergents, paper, artificial fibres (rayon), de-greasing metals and in petroleum refining.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bleaching powder — calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime; used for disinfecting water and bleaching cotton and paper.

• Borax — sodium tetraborate decahydrate, Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O; used in glass, ceramics and as a cleaning agent (borax bead test).

• Chalk — calcium carbonate, CaCO₃; also the composition of limestone and marble.

NOTE

• Common names: Washing soda — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O; Baking soda — NaHCO₃; Quicklime — CaO; Slaked lime — Ca(OH)₂; Plaster of Paris — CaSO₄·½H₂O; Gypsum — CaSO₄·2H₂O.

• Epsom salt — MgSO₄·7H₂O; Blue vitriol — CuSO₄·5H₂O; Green vitriol — FeSO₄·7H₂O; Laughing gas — N₂O; Dry ice — solid CO₂.

question: Which country is the leading producer of coffee in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brazil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Brazil has been the world's largest producer and exporter of coffee for over 150 years, accounting for roughly one-third of global output. (ब्राज़ील — कॉफी उत्पादन में प्रथम)

• Coffee in Brazil is grown mainly in Minas Gerais, São Paulo and Espírito Santo on the fertile *terra rossa* soils; the plantations are locally called fazendas.

• Coffee is a tropical plantation crop requiring hot–humid climate, well-drained loamy soil on hill slopes, and shade; the two main varieties are Arabica and Robusta.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• After Brazil, the leading coffee producers are Vietnam, Colombia, Indonesia and Ethiopia; coffee is believed to have originated in Ethiopia.

• India ranks around 7th–8th in world coffee production; within India, Karnataka is the largest producer (Chikmagalur, Coorg/Kodagu, Hassan), followed by Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

• The Coffee Board of India (headquartered at Bengaluru) works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

NOTE

• India's coffee: about 70% Robusta and 30% Arabica; famous varieties are Monsooned Malabar and Coorg Arabica (GI-tagged).

• World leaders: Tea — China (India 2nd); Rice and Wheat — China (India 2nd); Sugarcane — Brazil; Milk, Pulses, Jute and Spices — India.

question: Which of the following books is written by Mulk Raj Anand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Untouchable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Untouchable (1935) is the celebrated novel by Mulk Raj Anand, describing a single day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper, and exposing the evils of untouchability. (अछूत — मुल्कराज आनंद)

• Mulk Raj Anand was a pioneer of Indian English fiction; his other works include Coolie, Two Leaves and a Bud, The Village, Across the Black Waters, The Sword and the Sickle and The Private Life of an Indian Prince.

• He was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award (1971) and the Padma Bhushan (1967).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The English Teacher — by R.K. Narayan, the third of his Malgudi novels along with *Swami and Friends* and *The Bachelor of Arts*; he also wrote *The Guide* (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1960).

• The Blue Umbrella — by Ruskin Bond, who also wrote *The Room on the Roof* and *A Flight of Pigeons*.

• A Suitable Boy — by Vikram Seth, who also wrote *The Golden Gate* and *An Equal Music*.

NOTE

• The "big three" of early Indian English fiction: Mulk Raj Anand, R.K. Narayan and Raja Rao (*Kanthapura*).

• Other author–book pairs: *Midnight's Children* — Salman Rushdie; *The God of Small Things* — Arundhati Roy; *The White Tiger* — Aravind Adiga; *Train to Pakistan* — Khushwant Singh; *Interpreter of Maladies* — Jhumpa Lahiri.

question: Confluence of Bhagirathi and Alaknanda occur at ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devaprayag.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet at Devprayag in Tehri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, and from this point the river is known as the Ganga. (देवप्रयाग)

• The Bhagirathi rises from the Gangotri glacier (Gaumukh) and the Alaknanda rises near the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers above Badrinath.

• Devprayag is the last and most important of the Panch Prayag (five confluences) of the Alaknanda.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vishnuprayag — Alaknanda meets the Dhauliganga.

• Nandaprayag — Alaknanda meets the Nandakini.

• Rudraprayag — Alaknanda meets the Mandakini; Karnaprayag — Alaknanda meets the Pindar.

NOTE

• Order of the Panch Prayag from upstream to downstream: Vishnuprayag → Nandaprayag → Karnaprayag → Rudraprayag → Devprayag.

• The Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar; it is joined by the Yamuna at Prayagraj (Allahabad), and forms the Sundarbans delta with the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) and Meghna.

• The Ganga was declared India's National River in 2008; Namami Gange programme was launched in 2014.

question: In the Indian Judicial system, PIL stands for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public Interest Litigation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PIL stands for Public Interest Litigation — a litigation filed in a court of law for the protection of the public interest, not for the personal gain of the petitioner. (जनहित याचिका)

• It relaxes the traditional rule of locus standi, so that any public-spirited person can approach the Supreme Court under Article 32 or a High Court under Article 226 on behalf of those unable to do so.

• PIL was introduced in India in the late 1970s–80s mainly through Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer; *Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979)* on undertrial prisoners is regarded as the first reported PIL case.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PILs commonly concern environmental protection, human rights, prison and police reform, bonded labour, corruption and consumer welfare.

• Courts may impose exemplary costs on frivolous or motivated PILs to prevent misuse ("publicity interest litigation").

• The other three options are not legal terms used in the Indian judicial system.

NOTE

• Article 32 — Right to Constitutional Remedies, called the "heart and soul of the Constitution" by Dr B.R. Ambedkar; five writs — *Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo-Warranto*.

• Landmark PILs: *M.C. Mehta* cases (Ganga pollution, Taj Trapezium, CNG in Delhi), *Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)* on sexual harassment at the workplace.

question: Which of the following is one of the Trustees of the PM CARES Fund?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shri Ratan N. Tata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shri Ratan N. Tata was nominated as a Trustee of the PM CARES Fund (along with Justice K.T. Thomas and Shri Kariya Munda) in 2022. (पीएम केयर्स फंड)

• PM CARES stands for Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund; it was set up on 27 March 2020 to deal with the COVID-19 pandemic and similar emergencies.

• Its ex-officio Trustees are the Prime Minister (Chairperson) and the Ministers of Defence, Home Affairs and Finance; it is a public charitable trust and donations qualify for 100% deduction under Section 80G and count as CSR expenditure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ratan Tata — Chairman Emeritus of Tata Sons; awarded the Padma Bhushan (2000) and the Padma Vibhushan (2008).

• Azim Premji — of Wipro, known for the Azim Premji Foundation and for signing the Giving Pledge; Padma Vibhushan (2011).

• Mukesh Ambani — Chairman of Reliance Industries; Gautam Adani — Chairman of the Adani Group. Neither is a PM CARES trustee.

NOTE

• The older Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) was set up in 1948 by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, originally to help displaced persons from Pakistan.

• PM CARES funds were used for ventilators, PSA oxygen plants, vaccine development and the PM CARES for Children scheme (2021) for children orphaned by COVID-19.

question: Which Mauryan ruler was called Amitrochates by the Greeks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bindusara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bindusara (c. 297–273 BCE), son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of Ashoka, was called Amitrochates by the Greeks — from the Sanskrit Amitraghata, meaning "slayer of foes". (अमित्रघात — बिन्दुसार)

• He is also mentioned as Allitrochades and, in Jain texts, as Simhasena; he followed the Ajivika sect.

• Deimachus was sent as an ambassador to his court by Antiochus I of Syria; Bindusara famously asked for sweet wine, dried figs and a sophist (philosopher).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Samudragupta — Gupta ruler called the "Indian Napoleon" (by V.A. Smith); his exploits are recorded in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) composed by Harisena.

• Kanishka — the greatest Kushana ruler; started the Saka era in 78 CE and convened the Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvana, Kashmir.

• Chandragupta I — founder of the Gupta empire's greatness; he married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi and took the title Maharajadhiraja.

NOTE

• Mauryan dynasty: Chandragupta Maurya (322 BCE) → Bindusara → Ashoka → ... → Brihadratha (last, killed by Pushyamitra Sunga).

• Megasthenes, ambassador of Seleucus Nicator, visited Chandragupta Maurya's court and wrote Indica; Kautilya's Arthashastra is the key Mauryan text.

question: With respect to social groups in India, PVTGs stands for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PVTGs stands for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups — the most marginalised sub-category among the Scheduled Tribes. (विशेष रूप से कमजोर जनजातीय समूह)

• They were earlier known as Primitive Tribal Groups (PTGs), a category created on the recommendation of the Dhebar Commission (1960–61); the name was changed to PVTGs in 2006.

• There are 75 PVTGs spread over 18 States and the UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands; Odisha has the largest number (13).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Criteria for identification as a PVTG: pre-agricultural level of technology, stagnant or declining population, extremely low literacy, and subsistence-level economy.

• Examples: Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese and Shompen (A&N Islands), Birhor and Sabar (Jharkhand), Bondo, Juang and Dongria Kondh (Odisha), Toda and Kota (Tamil Nadu), Cholanaikayan and Kadar (Kerala).

• The nodal ministry is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (created in 1999).

NOTE

• PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), launched in 2023, targets the development of PVTG households and habitations.

• Constitutional provisions for STs: Article 342 (specification of STs), Article 244 with the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, Article 338A (National Commission for Scheduled Tribes).

question: Kathak classical dance had its origin in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kathak originated in Uttar Pradesh, evolving from the storytelling of the wandering bards called Kathakars who narrated epics through gesture, song and dance. (कथक — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• The word Kathak comes from "katha" meaning story; it is the only classical dance strongly influenced by Mughal/Persian court traditions, and is marked by rapid footwork (tatkar), chakkars (spins) and intricate rhythmic patterns.

• Its three main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras (with Raigarh as a later gharana).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rajasthan — home of folk dances such as Ghoomar, Kalbelia (UNESCO ICH), Chari, Kachhi Ghodi and Bhavai; the Jaipur gharana of Kathak also flourished here.

• Odisha — home of the classical dance Odissi, and folk dances such as Chhau (Mayurbhanj) and Ghumura.

• Assam — home of the classical dance Sattriya, founded by Srimanta Sankardeva, and the folk dance Bihu.

NOTE

• Kathak exponents: Pt. Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj, Gopi Krishna, Kumudini Lakhia.

• Kathak is the only major classical dance form performed by both Hindu and Muslim artists; it was accorded classical status by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

question: In a drama, Hema spoke "Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it". Which Indian freedom fighter gave this slogan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous slogan "Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it" was given by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, who was hailed as Lokmanya and called the "Father of Indian Unrest" by Valentine Chirol. (स्वराज्य मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है)

• Tilak was one of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio of extremist leaders (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal); he started the festivals Ganapati (1893) and Shivaji (1895) to mobilise people.

• He founded the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English), and started the All India Home Rule League in April 1916 at Belgaum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mahatma Gandhi — gave the slogans "Do or Die (Karo ya Maro)" during the Quit India Movement (1942) and "Satyagraha"; he was called the Father of the Nation.

• Ambika Charan Majumdar — moderate leader who presided over the 1916 Lucknow session of the Congress, at which the Congress and the Muslim League signed the Lucknow Pact and the two Congress factions reunited.

• Bhagat Singh — revolutionary of the HSRA who popularised "Inquilab Zindabad"; hanged on 23 March 1931 with Rajguru and Sukhdev.

NOTE

• Famous slogans: "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan" — Lal Bahadur Shastri; "Dilli Chalo" and "Tum Mujhe Khoon Do, Main Tumhe Azadi Dunga" — Subhas Chandra Bose; "Vande Mataram" — Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay; "Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna" — Bismil Azimabadi (popularised by Ram Prasad Bismil).

• Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya and The Arctic Home in the Vedas while imprisoned in Mandalay jail (1908–14).
